cards.title: Local search & optimisation problems
cards.hook: When there are too many possibilities (20! ≈ 2.4×10¹⁸ routes), improve one candidate step by step.
cards.visual:
Search problemLocal search / optimisation
state spacerange of decision variables + constraints
transition functionsuccessor (neighbour) function
goal testobjective f = min(cost) or max(fit)
path mattersonly the final state matters
example: Delivery: STATE = route, NEIGHBOUR = swap two stops, OBJECTIVE = minimise distance, CONSTRAINT = visit once.
cards.trap: Local search doesn't return a path; it returns the best state found.
explain: Sometimes we don't care HOW we get to a solution, only how GOOD the final answer is. Planning a delivery route over 20 customers has 20! ≈ 2.4 × 10¹⁸ possible routes, far too many to check one by one.

Local search keeps one (or a few) complete candidate solutions and keeps tweaking them to make them better. Each candidate is a state; small tweaks give neighbours; an objective function scores each state.
8-queens: a state lists the row of the queen in each column; the cost counts pairs of queens attacking each other. A goal state has cost 0 (there are 92 of them).

cards.title: Hill climbing
cards.hook: Keep walking uphill while the next step improves your height.
cards.visual:
StepAction
1start anywhere
2generate neighbours
3move to the best improving neighbour
4stop when no neighbour is better (a peak)
example: 8-queens state with h = 17; best successor cost 12 → move there.
cards.memory: Greedy uphill, one step at a time.
cards.trap: It can stop at a LOCAL maximum (or plateau), not the global best.
explain: Hill climbing is like walking up a hill in thick fog: you can only see the ground right around you, so you always step in the direction that goes up the most.
It looks at all neighbours, moves to the best one if it is better than where you are, and stops when no neighbour is better. It's fast and simple.
The danger: it stops at the first peak it finds, which may only be a local maximum (a small hill), not the highest mountain.

cards.title: Simulated annealing
cards.hook: Like cooling metal slowly: shake a lot when hot, settle when cold.
example: Δ = 2, T = 5: p = e^(−0.4) = 0.670 → accept if random r < 0.670.
cards.memory: Hot = Happy to explore; Cold = Careful.
cards.trap: Cooling too fast behaves like hill climbing; too slow needs many iterations. No guarantee of the best in one run.
explain: Simulated annealing copies how metal is hardened: heat it, then cool it slowly so the atoms settle into a strong, low-energy arrangement.

Like hill climbing it tries a neighbour, but it will sometimes accept a WORSE move. When the temperature T is high it accepts bad moves often (exploring); as T cools it becomes picky (settling). This lets it escape small hills that would trap hill climbing.
Better moves are always accepted. Worse moves (worse by Δ) are accepted with probability e^(−Δ/T).

where: how much worse the neighbour is (energy increase)
current temperature from the cooling schedule

cards.title: Genetic algorithms
cards.hook: Evolve a population: the fitter breed more, children mix and mutate.
cards.memory: Select, Cross, Mutate (and keep the Elite).
cards.trap: Roulette: even weak individuals can be chosen (if fitness > 0); one very fit individual may dominate.
explain: A genetic algorithm imitates evolution. It keeps a whole population of candidate solutions. Fitter candidates are more likely to become parents; parents swap parts (crossover); children occasionally change randomly (mutation).
Roulette wheel: each individual gets a slice of a wheel proportional to its fitness; spin to pick a parent. Tournament: pick k at random and take the fittest.
Over generations the population drifts toward better solutions while mutation keeps diversity.
